sections.title: Talking about pets
sections.content: *állat* ("animal") and *háziállat* ("pet", literally a "house animal") are the two new words here. You know *kutya*, *macska* and *madár* from A1, and *hal* too. You also know *Van egy kutyám* ("I have a dog") from A1: *van* plus the possessive ending is how Hungarian says "to have". So you can already say which pets you have.

items.spanish: Van egy kicsi kutyám és egy nagy macskám.
items.english: I have a small dog and a big cat.

items.spanish: A kutya és a macska háziállat.
items.english: A dog and a cat are pets.

sections.content: After a number the noun stays singular, as you know from A1: *két macska* ("two cats"), never *két macskák*. The same goes for *sok háziállat* ("many pets").
